To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
atherosclerosis is an inflammatory process and the inflammatory process plays an important role.
Inflammation plays a key role in the initiation of atherosclerosis, and the inflammatory process is associated with plaque vulnerability and instability.

1) inflammatory mechanisms are involved in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis; 2) atherosclerotic plaque rupture and clinical events are associated with an inflammatory phenotype; 3) T cell mediated responses and expression of cytokines/chemokines are important inflammatory mechanisms; 4) anti-inflammatory mechanisms are also involved; 5) anti-inflammatory markers are associated with plaque stability and clinical outcome; 6) current management involves both mechanical and pharmacotherapy aimed at suppressing the inflammatory mechanisms
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inflammatory processes in atherosclerotic lesions and the clinical consequences.
the role of T lymphocytes in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and the potential of T cell directed immunomodulation in the prevention of atherosclerosis.
the role of T cells in atherosclerosis and their interaction with endothelial cells, macrophages and smooth muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inflammation is central in the initiation and development of atherosclerosis and that the inflammatory response can also be targeted for therapeutic benefit.
inflammation plays a key role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerotic disease and that the identification of novel inflammatory markers may help identify patients who are at risk of clinical events.
inflammation is a key component of the atherosclerotic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inflammation plays an important role not only in the initiation and development of atherosclerosis, but also in the destabilisation and progression towards clinical events.

inflammation plays an important role at different stages of atherosclerosis and that the balance between pro- and anti- inflammatory mediators is crucial for the development and progression of atheroma.
inflammation plays a key role in atherosclerosis and that the inflammatory process is not only a cause but a consequence of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pro- and the anti-inflammatory processes are not mutually exclusive and are rather complementary.
atherosclerosis, the underlying inflammatory process, and clinical implications are closely related.
atherosclerosis is an inflammatory disease and the inflammatory process is the key to understanding its pathophysiology.
